bridges.statement: The historical evidence supports answering yes to whether Jesus rose from the dead.
Reliable burial and five converging considerations establish that Jesus' tomb was empty.
Divine resurrection best explains the complete evidence under comparative historical criteria.
The unexpected origin of specifically resurrection belief requires more than existing Jewish expectations.
Pauline bodily transformation and individual and group appearances support physical resurrection.
The Gospels' biographical genre and source use permit reliance on their historical core.

routes.speaker: Richard Carrier
routes.position: Denies that the historical evidence establishes resurrection over natural explanations.

bridges.statement: Natural explanations remain preferable unless exceptional evidence rules them out.
The evidence neither securely establishes a missing body nor excludes ordinary missing-body causes.
Gospel dependence and symbolic literary construction defeat their use as independent historical proof.
The Epistles establish visionary claims, not an emptied grave or supernatural event.
Craig has not shown evidence exceptional enough to overcome resurrection's prior improbability.
Scripture, eschatological expectation, and visionary experience naturally explain resurrection belief.
